answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying minting rights to verifiable useful work: each identity earns a small, non-transferable quota only after completing tasks that peers independently verify, like a sonnet judged on meter rather than claimed authorship. Quotas decay if unused, and duplicate work across identities is flagged because outputs are hashed into a public ivory ledger, a mirror that exposes copy-paste farming. Creating a thousand fake agents gains nothing, since each must pay the same real work cost before it can act.
